title.value: Public Perspectives on Exposure Notification Apps: A Patient and Citizen Co-Designed Study
title.justification: The title reflects the focus on public perspectives and co-designed methodologies related to exposure notification apps.
title.quote: Public Perspectives on Exposure Notification Apps: A Patient and Citizen Co-Designed Study

extractions.description: This paper discusses a study on the public's perspectives on the COVID Alert exposure notification app, deployed in Canada. The study highlights the use, knowledge, concerns, and predictors of app downloads among the public in Quebec, as well as strategies to promote social acceptability. The paper emphasizes the importance of public engagement in app development to improve uptake and effectiveness.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on public health communication and technology adoption, rather than directly addressing climate or ecological sustainability.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Our aims are to (1) assess the use, knowledge, and concerns of the COVID Alert app, (2) identify predictors of app downloads, and (3) develop strategies to promote social acceptability.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily deals with public health communication and technology for disease control, which does not directly fit into any climate or ecological sustainable development category.
primary_category.quote: The study object was the COVID Alert app, from the perspective of Québec residents.

secondary_categories.justification: There are no secondary themes related to climate or ecological sustainable development.
secondary_categories.quote: The experience gained through the introduction of this tool during the COVID-19 pandemic can also inform the responsible development and deployment of future digital health interventions.

primary_sub_category.justification: The study focuses on a public health app rather than an environmental or sustainability sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: COVID Alert’s failure to launch, as noted for other exposure notification apps as well, may seem surprising given the initial interest in this technology and the substantial threats to population health and civil liberties.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper remains focused on public health and technology without significant crossover into environmental topics.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: While some studies have demonstrated effectiveness in particular settings, the real-life effectiveness of digital contact tracing and exposure notification remains limited.

new_primary_category.justification: The paper does not introduce a new sustainable development category but focuses on public health and technology.
new_primary_category.quote: Canada deployed a digital exposure notification app (COVID Alert) as a strategy to support manual contact tracing.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: There is no new sub-category introduced as the content revolves around public health rather than environmental developments.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: Our survey found significant gaps in user knowledge about the app and its functionalities.
